Hi all,

Attaching our preliminary evidence bundle and a short attestation. The attached ZIP contains: SIG-Redwood-response-2025.pdf (control mappings), redwood-eu-vpc-network-diagram.png, and an evidence-index.csv that maps files to SIG control IDs.

Quick notes on the residency controls:
- For EU-only processing we rely on region pinning at the routing layer plus KV cache sharding to EU nodes. This prevents model KV cache eviction to non-EU hosts for pinned tenants.
- Logs: we can route audit logs to EU storage buckets and restrict retention per your policy. Physical media encryption uses AES-256; we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) hosted in an EU KMS or Redwood-managed EU CMKs.
- SOC2: our latest report (2024-Q4) includes control descriptions for logical and physical access in our EU regions; the SOC2 report redactions are standard — we provide a SOC2 summary and a SOC2 bridge letter on request.

Caveats:
- If Medilabs requires an air-gapped or on-prem enclave, that is out of scope for hosted teams; we can discuss Redwood Private as an alternative (longer lead time and on-prem packaging).
- Cross-border model updates: model checkpoint pushes may traverse a centralized model store. For EU-only tenancy we can pin runtime to EU clones; please declare whether model updates from non-EU build pipelines are acceptable or need review.

Next step: Lauren / Monica — propose we set a technical kickoff this week to align on KMS choice and peering method. Oliver — let us know which of the two options you prefer (VPC peering with route tables vs Private Connect with static IPs).

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
